0225 [PARA] Normal                         | 📏 TYPES OF ANTHROPOMETRIC MEASUREMENTS
0226 [PARA] Normal                         | 1. Length vs Height
0227 [PARA] Normal                         | Length: Measured lying down (0–2 years)
0228 [PARA] Normal                         | Height: Measured standing (>2 years)
0229 [PARA] Normal                         | 2. Weight
0230 [PARA] Normal                         | Measured using calibrated infant or adult scales
0231 [PARA] Normal                         | Compared to weight-for-age standards
0232 [PARA] Normal                         | 3. Head Circumference (OFC)
0233 [PARA] Normal                         | Measures brain growth (0–3 years)
0234 [PARA] Normal                         | Measured at widest part of forehead and occipital bone
0235 [PARA] Normal                         | 4. Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC)
0236 [PARA] Normal                         | Indicates acute malnutrition (children 6–59 months)
0237 [PARA] Normal                         | Measured at midpoint between shoulder and elbow (left arm)

0264 [PARA] Normal                         |  MNEMONICS FOR ANTHROPOMETRY
0265 [PARA] Normal                         | Mnemonic: “WHO BMI”
0266 [PARA] Normal                         | W: Weight-for-age → Underweight
0267 [PARA] Normal                         | H: Height-for-age → Stunting
0268 [PARA] Normal                         | O: Obesity/BMI-for-age → Overnutrition
0269 [PARA] Normal                         | BMI: Weight / Height² → Adult classification
0270 [PARA] Normal                         | Chest circumference:
0271 [PARA] Normal                         | Measure at the nipple level and ensure the tape is taut.
0272 [PARA] Normal                         | Is 2- 4cm < OFC at birth.
0273 [PARA] Normal                         | Equal with OFC at lyr.
0274 [PARA] Normal                         | After 1yr. CC >OFC.
0275 [PARA] Normal                         | 
0276 [PARA] Normal                         |  Head > Chest at birth → Normal
0277 [PARA] Normal                         |   Chest = Head at ~1 year
0278 [PARA] Normal                         |   Chest > Head after 1 year
0279 [PARA] Normal                         |   Chest-to-OFC ratio <1 after 1 year = Red flag
0280 [PARA] Normal                         |

0284 [PARA] Normal                         | WFH → Wasted

0522 [PARA] Normal                         | 🛢️ WHAT IS KEROSENE POISONING?
0523 [PARA] Normal                         | Kerosene poisoning is a form of hydrocarbon poisoning, commonly seen in children under 5 years due to accidental ingesti
0524 [PARA] Normal                         | 
0525 [PARA] Normal                         |  COMPOSITION OF KEROSENE
0526 [PARA] Normal                         | A low-viscosity, volatile petroleum hydrocarbon
0527 [PARA] Normal                         | Contains aliphatic hydrocarbons
0528 [PARA] Normal                         | Easily aspirated due to low surface tension and high volatility
0529 [PARA] Normal                         | 
0530 [PARA] Normal                         | 🔬 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY
0531 [PARA] Normal                         | The primary danger of kerosene ingestion is aspiration pneumonitis, not systemic toxicity.
0532 [PARA] Normal                         | 📉 Sequence:
0533 [PARA] Normal                         | Ingestion → triggers gag/cough reflex
0534 [PARA] Normal                         | Aspiration into lungs → chemical pneumonitis
0535 [PARA] Normal                         | Pulmonary surfactant is destroyed
0536 [PARA] Normal                         | Alveolar damage → inflammation → hypoxia
0537 [PARA] Normal                         | 
0538 [PARA] Normal                         |  MNEMONIC: “KERO” for dangers
0539 [PARA] Normal                         | K – Kills surfactant
0540 [PARA] Normal                         | E – Enters lungs easily (aspiration risk)
0541 [PARA] Normal                         | R – Respiratory symptoms dominate
0542 [PARA] Normal                         | O – Oil-based chemical pneumonitis
0543 [PARA] Normal                         | 
0544 [PARA] Normal                         | ⚠️ CLINICAL FEATURES
0545 [PARA] Normal                         |  Pulmonary (most important)
0546 [PARA] Normal                         | Cough, tachypnea
0547 [PARA] Normal                         | Grunting, nasal flaring
0548 [PARA] Normal                         | Cyanosis
0549 [PARA] Normal                         | Crepitations (crackles) on auscultation
0550 [PARA] Normal                         | 🌡️ Gastrointestinal
0551 [PARA] Normal                         | Nausea, vomiting
0552 [PARA] Normal                         | Abdominal pain
0553 [PARA] Normal                         |  CNS
0554 [PARA] Normal                         | Drowsiness, lethargy
0555 [PARA] Normal                         | Occasionally convulsions (rare, due to hypoxia)

1231 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Excreted into bile → intestine → stool
1232 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | ⚠️ Neonates have:
1233 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Increased RBC breakdown
1234 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Immature liver enzymes
1235 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Increased enterohepatic circulation
1236 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | → Predisposing to jaundice

2096 [PARA] Heading 3                      | ✅ Etiology:
2097 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Rh(D) incompatibility (most common)
2098 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Mother: Rh-negative
2099 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Fetus: Rh-positive
2100 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Maternal sensitization → Anti-D IgG antibodies cross placenta → hemolysis of fetal RBCs
2101 [PARA] Heading 3                      | ✅ Pathophysiology:
2102 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Fetal hemolysis → severe anemia → high-output cardiac failure → fluid accumulation → hydrops
2103 [PARA] Heading 3                      | ✅ Prevention:
2104 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Anti-D immunoglobulin (Rho(D) immune globulin) prophylaxis to Rh-negative mothers at 28 weeks and after delivery.

3235 [PARA] Normal                         | SPINA BIFIDA 
3236 [PARA] Normal                         | Spina bifida is a type of neural tube defect (NTD) in which there is incomplete closure of the embryonic neural tube, re
3237 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Embryology
3238 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | The neural tube forms between the 3rd and 4th weeks of gestation.
3239 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Failure of the caudal (lower) end of the neural tube to close properly results in spina bifida.
3240 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Can be due to genetic, nutritional (especially folate deficiency), or environmental factors.
3241 [PARA] Normal                         | Types of Spina Bifida
3242 [PARA] Normal                         | Spina Bifida Occulta (Hidden Form)
3243 [PARA] Normal                         | Most mild and common form.
3244 [PARA] Normal                         | Vertebral arches fail to fuse but the spinal cord and meninges remain in place.
3245 [PARA] Normal                         | Skin over the defect is usually intact and may have:
3246 [PARA] Normal                         | Tuft of hair
3247 [PARA] Normal                         | Dermal sinus
3248 [PARA] Normal                         | Lipoma
3249 [PARA] Normal                         | Dimple
3250 [PARA] Normal                         | No herniation of neural tissue.
3251 [PARA] Normal                         | Clinical Features:
3252 [PARA] Normal                         | Often asymptomatic.
3253 [PARA] Normal                         | May later present with:
3254 [PARA] Normal                         | Tethered cord syndrome
3255 [PARA] Normal                         | Weakness or sensory loss in lower limbs
3256 [PARA] Normal                         | Urinary incontinence
3257 [PARA] Normal                         | Meningocele
3258 [PARA] Normal                         | Meninges herniate through the bony defect, forming a CSF-filled sac.
3259 [PARA] Normal                         | Spinal cord remains in place.
3260 [PARA] Normal                         | Neurological function is usually preserved.
3261 [PARA] Normal                         | Clinical Features:
3262 [PARA] Normal                         | Cystic swelling over the spine (usually lumbar/sacral).
3263 [PARA] Normal                         | Covered by thin skin or meninges.
3264 [PARA] Normal                         | Minimal or no neurological deficits.
3265 [PARA] Normal                         | Myelomeningocele (Open Spina Bifida)
3266 [PARA] Normal                         | Most severe and common symptomatic form.
3267 [PARA] Normal                         | Both meninges and spinal cord herniate through the defect.
3268 [PARA] Normal                         | Sac may rupture, exposing neural tissue to the environment.
3269 [TABLE] 5x4                            | Type | Defect | Clinical Features | Covering

3271 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Occulta Meningocele Myelomeningocele Myeloschisis

3279 [PARA] Normal                         | Bladder and bowel dysfunction.

3297 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | 400–800 mcg/day (low-risk)
3298 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | 4 mg/day (high-risk women, e.g., previous NTD baby, epilepsy)
3299 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   |   Avoid teratogenic drugs and control maternal diabetes.

4400 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Presents in adulthood (30s–40s)

4402 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Slowly progressive → leads to end-stage renal disease (ESRD)
4403 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Autosomal Recessive PKD (ARPKD)
4404 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Rare; presents in infancy or early childhood
4405 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | More severe → often associated with pulmonary hypoplasia and congenital hepatic fibrosis
4406 [PARA] Normal                         |

4411 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Progressive renal failure (usually by 60 years)

4413 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Liver cysts (most common)

4415 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Mitral valve prolapse
4416 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Pancreatic and splenic cysts

4421 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | I – Infections (recurrent UTIs, cyst infections)
4422 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | N – Nephrolithiasis (kidney stones, common)
4423 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | S – Size ↑ of kidneys (palpable abdominal masses)
4424 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | H – Hypertension (early and common)
4425 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | L – Liver cysts (most common extrarenal manifestation)
4426 [PARA] Normal                         |

4440 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 🔹 Management

4442 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Control blood pressure (ACE inhibitors/ARBs)

4445 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Avoid nephrotoxins and maintain hydration

5338 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 🟦 ACYANOTIC HEART DEFECTS
5339 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Mnemonic: "Loud Murmur, Pink Baby" (Left-to-right shunts → ↑ Pulmonary flow, but no cyanosis)
5340 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 1. Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD)
5341 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Thrill at left lower sternal border
5342 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Harsh pansystolic murmur at LLSB
5343 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Signs of heart failure (tachypnea, hepatomegaly)
5344 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Normal oxygen saturation
5345 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 2. Atrial Septal Defect (ASD)
5346 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Wide fixed split of S2
5347 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Systolic ejection murmur (due to ↑ flow across pulmonary valve)
5348 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Right ventricular heave
5349 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | May have a soft mid-diastolic murmur (tricuspid flow)
5350 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 3. Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA)
5351 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Continuous "machinery" murmur at left upper sternal border
5352 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Bounding peripheral pulses
5353 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Wide pulse pressure
5354 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Displaced apex beat in large shunts
5355 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 4. Coarctation of Aorta
5356 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Radiofemoral delay
5357 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Upper limb hypertension
5358 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Weak or absent femoral pulses
5359 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Systolic murmur at back (interscapular region)
5360 [PARA] Normal                         | 
5361 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 🟪 CYANOTIC HEART DEFECTS
5362 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Mnemonic: "Blue Baby, Quiet Murmur" (Right-to-left shunts → ↓ Pulmonary flow → Cyanosis)
5363 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 1. Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF)
5364 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Central cyanosis, especially on exertion
5365 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Ejection systolic murmur at left upper sternal border (due to pulmonary stenosis)
5366 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Single S2
5367 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Clubbing (after 6 months)
5368 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Squatting posture (relieves hypoxia)
5369 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 2. Transposition of the Great Arteries (TGA)
5370 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Profound central cyanosis at birth
5371 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | No murmur (unless VSD or PDA present)
5372 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Loud S2
5373 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Signs of shock and acidosis if no mixing lesion
5374 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 3. Truncus Arteriosus
5375 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Mild cyanosis
5376 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Single loud S2
5377 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Systolic murmur (from associated VSD)
5378 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Signs of CHF by 1–2 weeks of age
5379 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 4. Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return (TAPVR)
5380 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Cyanosis, especially in obstructed type
5381 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Right heart failure signs
5382 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Fixed split S2, systolic murmur
5383 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Hepatomegaly
5384 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Often critically ill neonate if obstructed
5385 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 5. Tricuspid Atresia
5386 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Severe cyanosis, single S2
5387 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Murmur (if VSD present)
5388 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Left ventricular heave
5389 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Polycythemia (later)
5390 [PARA] Normal                         |

5554 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is there projectile vomiting (non-bilious)? → Pyloric stenosis
5555 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is vomiting bilious (green)? → Duodenal/intestinal atresia, malrotation with volvulus

5557 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Abdominal distension or visible loops? → Intestinal obstruction, Hirschsprung’s disease
5558 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any mass or defect at the umbilicus or abdomen at birth? → Omphalocele, gastroschisis
5559 [PARA] Heading 3                      | C. Stooling Patterns
5560 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Did the baby pass meconium within 24–48 hours? → Delayed in: Hirschsprung’s disease, imperforate anus
5561 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is there constipation or ribbon-like stools? → Hirschsprung’s disease
5562 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any intermittent painless rectal bleeding? → Meckel’s diverticulum
5563 [PARA] Heading 3                      | D. Associated Symptoms
5564 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any recurrent chest infections or cough during feeds? → TEF
5565 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Signs of dehydration or poor feeding? → Pyloric stenosis
5566 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Poor weight gain or failure to thrive?

5927 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 🔍 QUESTIONS TO RULE OUT CAUSES
5928 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 1. Genetic/Syndromic Causes
5929 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is there any family history of similar malformations?
5930 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Are the parents related (consanguinity)?
5931 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has any genetic testing been done?
5932 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Are there any other abnormalities noticed in the child (e.g., heart problems, vision/hearing issues)?
5933 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Does the child look different from other children (facial features, body proportions)?
5934 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any known syndromes in the family (e.g., Trisomy 13, Apert, Pierre Robin)?
5935 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 2. Environmental/Teratogenic Causes
5936 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Did the mother take any medications during pregnancy (especially antiepileptics, retinoic acid)?
5937 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Was there any exposure to alcohol, smoking, or drugs during pregnancy?
5938 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any illnesses during pregnancy, especially:
5939 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Rubella
5940 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Toxoplasmosis
5941 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Cytomegalovirus (CMV)
5942 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Syphilis
5943 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Diabetes mellitus
5944 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any history of radiation exposure during pregnancy?
5945 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Was the pregnancy associated with oligohydramnios (may contribute to clubfoot)?
5946 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 3. Mechanical/Positional Factors
5947 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Was the baby in a breech position?
5948 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any multiple gestations (e.g., twins)?
5949 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Was there reduced amniotic fluid (oligohydramnios)?
5950 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Was the child’s position in utero ever described as unusual?

5952 [PARA] Heading 2                      | ⚠️ QUESTIONS TO IDENTIFY COMPLICATIONS
5953 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 🦶 For Clubfoot:
5954 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is the child able to stand or walk normally?
5955 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is there any limping, pain, or imbalance?
5956 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is one leg/foot shorter or smaller than the other?
5957 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any pressure sores or skin changes on the foot?
5958 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has the child had multiple recurrences after treatment?
5959 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 🖐️ For Polydactyly/Syndactyly:
5960 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Does the child have difficulty using the hand or foot?
5961 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any pain during movement?
5962 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any signs of joint stiffness or abnormal bone growth?
5963 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 👄 For Cleft Lip and/or Palate:
5964 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is the child having difficulty feeding, especially during infancy?
5965 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any history of choking, nasal regurgitation, or poor weight gain?
5966 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has the child had ear infections or hearing loss?
5967 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is there any nasal speech or speech delay?
5968 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any issues with teeth alignment or jaw development?
5969 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 🌍 General Complications (all malformations):
5970 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has the child been socially excluded or stigmatized?
5971 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has the condition affected schooling or developmental progress?
5972 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any psychological distress in child or parents?

5976 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 🦶 MUSCULOSKELETAL MALFORMATIONS
5977 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 1. Congenital Talipes Equinovarus (Clubfoot)
5978 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Inspection:
5979 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Foot appears inverted and plantar-flexed ("equinovarus").
5980 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Medial convexity, lateral concavity of the foot.
5981 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Deep medial skin crease.
5982 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Calf muscle may appear smaller on affected side.
5983 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Check for bilateral or unilateral involvement.
5984 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Palpation:
5985 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Assess tendo-Achilles tightness.
5986 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Foot feels stiff (rigid) or flexible (positional).
5987 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Check temperature and skin integrity (for complications like pressure sores).
5988 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Functional:
5989 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Observe gait (if child is walking) – may walk on outer edge of foot or toes.
5990 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Assess range of motion of ankle and subtalar joints.
5991 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Associated signs:
5992 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Look for signs of neuromuscular conditions (e.g., spina bifida, hypotonia).
5993 [PARA] Normal                         | 
5994 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 2. Polydactyly / Syndactyly
5995 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Inspection:
5996 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Count number of fingers/toes – note extra digits or fused ones.
5997 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Note location: preaxial (thumb side), postaxial (little finger side), or central.
5998 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Assess symmetry – bilateral or unilateral.
5999 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Look for associated nail anomalies.
6000 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Examine both hands and feet.
6001 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Palpation:
6002 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Assess bone vs soft tissue involvement in extra digits.
6003 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Check for joint movement and grip strength.
6004 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Evaluate for neurovascular sufficiency (capillary refill, pulses, sensation).
6005 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Functional:
6006 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Test fine motor skills, especially for hand anomalies.
6007 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Associated signs:
6008 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Look for dysmorphic features or signs of syndromes (e.g., Ellis-van Creveld, Carpenter syndrome).
6009 [PARA] Normal                         | 
6010 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 👄 CRANIOFACIAL MALFORMATIONS
6011 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 3. Cleft Lip and/or Palate
6012 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Inspection:
6013 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Obvious cleft of the upper lip, possibly extending into the nostril.
6014 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | For cleft palate: inspect inside the mouth, especially the hard and soft palate – may need tongue depressor and light.
6015 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Check for nasal deformity or asymmetry.
6016 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Check teeth alignment and gum ridge.
6017 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Palpation:
6018 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Gently palpate the palatal arch to feel for cleft (submucous clefts may be hidden).
6019 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Assess for notching of posterior palate.
6020 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Functional:
6021 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Listen to speech for nasality or articulation problems.
6022 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Observe for feeding difficulty or signs of failure to thrive.
6023 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Inspect ears for discharge, assess hearing (look for recurrent otitis media, middle ear effusion).
6024 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Associated signs:
6025 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Examine face for dysmorphic features or micrognathia.
6026 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Look for signs of Pierre Robin sequence, Treacher Collins syndrome, etc.
6027 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Check for airway obstruction, especially in babies.

6029 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 🔎 GENERAL/ASSOCIATED EXAMINATION
6030 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | In all cases, assess for:
6031 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Vital signs – especially growth parameters (weight, length, head circumference).
6032 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Cardiac examination – congenital anomalies may coexist (e.g., murmurs).
6033 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Neurological assessment – tone, reflexes, motor milestones.
6034 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Abdominal examination – for renal anomalies.
6035 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Spine – look for scoliosis, spina bifida signs.
6036 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Skin – for café-au-lait spots, hypopigmented patches, or other syndromic markers.

6045 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 🦶 1. CONGENITAL TALIPES EQUINOVARUS (CLUBFOOT)
6046 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 1. Inspection
6047 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Expose both lower limbs up to thighs.
6048 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Observe both feet from front, side, and back.
6049 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Look for:
6050 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Foot position: Equinus (plantarflexion), varus (inward rotation), adductus (forefoot inward), and cavus (high arch).
6051 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Skin creases: Deep medial or posterior crease.
6052 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Calf wasting (compare bilaterally).
6053 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Shoe wear pattern (in older children).
6054 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Signs of previous surgery/casting.
6055 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 2. Palpation
6056 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Warm hands.
6057 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Palpate:
6058 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Heel position (posterior displacement?).
6059 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Tight Achilles tendon.
6060 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Bony landmarks: Talus, calcaneus, navicular.
6061 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Temperature, skin condition, capillary refill.
6062 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 3. Manipulation/Movement
6063 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Assess range of motion at ankle and subtalar joints.
6064 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Try to passively correct deformity – assess rigidity vs flexibility.
6065 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 4. Function (if ambulatory)
6066 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Observe gait: toe-walking, lateral weight-bearing.
6067 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Check developmental milestones (if relevant).
6068 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 5. Additional
6069 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Examine spine and neurological status to rule out spina bifida or neuromuscular causes.
6070 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Check hip joint for developmental dysplasia.
6071 [PARA] Normal                         | 
6072 [PARA] Heading 2                      | ✋ 2. POLYDACTYLY / SYNDACTYLY
6073 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 1. Inspection
6074 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Inspect both hands and feet.
6075 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Note:
6076 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Number, position and size of extra digits.
6077 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Whether digit is fully formed or rudimentary.
6078 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Location: Preaxial, postaxial, or central.
6079 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | In syndactyly: number of digits fused and level (skin only vs bone).
6080 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Symmetry: bilateral vs unilateral.
6081 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 2. Palpation
6082 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Assess for:
6083 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Presence of bones vs soft tissue in extra digits.
6084 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Joint mobility in affected and adjacent digits.
6085 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Circulation: Capillary refill, pulse, temperature.
6086 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Sensory exam if child is old enough.
6087 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 3. Functional Assessment
6088 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Fine motor tasks: grasp, pick small objects, handwriting (if age-appropriate).
6089 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Compare grip strength bilaterally.
6090 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 4. Additional
6091 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Examine for other anomalies (e.g., facial features, heart sounds, renal anomalies).
6092 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Consider syndromic associations (e.g., Ellis-van Creveld).

6109 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Speech: Check for nasal speech, articulation issues.

6136 [PARA] Subtitle                       | FEBRILE SEIZURES
6137 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | A febrile seizure is a seizure associated with fever (≥38°C or 100.4°F) without evidence of CNS infection, metabolic dis
6138 [PARA] Normal                         | Pathophysiology
6139 [PARA] Normal                         | Immature brain more excitable
6140 [PARA] Normal                         | Fever lowers seizure threshold
6141 [PARA] Normal                         | Possibly due to genetic predisposition (e.g., SCN1A mutations)
6142 [PARA] Normal                         | Common viral infections: HHV-6 (roseola), influenza, adenovirus, enterovirus
6143 [PARA] Normal                         | Clinical Features
6144 [PARA] Normal                         | Occurs early in the illness, often within 24 hours of fever onset
6145 [PARA] Normal                         | Tonic-clonic movements, eye deviation, postictal sleepiness
6146 [PARA] Normal                         | No signs of meningism, focal neurological signs, or prolonged postictal state in simple type
6147 [PARA] Normal                         | Classification of Febrile Seizures

6306 [PARA] Normal                         | NEONATAL SEIZURES
6307 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | A neonatal seizure is a paroxysmal, involuntary disturbance of neurological function in a newborn, occurring within the 
6308 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Neonatal seizures are always a symptom of an underlying disorder and not a diagnosis in themselves.
6309 [PARA] Heading 2                      | WHY ARE NEONATAL SEIZURES UNIQUE?
6310 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | The neonatal brain is more excitable due to excess excitatory neurotransmitters (e.g., glutamate) and fewer inhibitory s
6311 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Classic tonic-clonic movements are rare.
6312 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Seizures are often subtle or focal due to immature myelination and incomplete cortical connectivity.
6313 [PARA] Heading 2                      | PATHOPHYSIOLOGY
6314 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | High brain excitability due to:
6315 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | ↑ NMDA and AMPA (excitatory receptors)
6316 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | ↓ GABA inhibition (paradoxically excitatory in neonates)
6317 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Immature neural networks → poor seizure spread → focal, fragmented seizures

6387 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 🧪 Essential:
6388 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Video EEG monitoring – gold standard
6389 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Shows no epileptic activity during typical events.
6390 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Psychiatric evaluation – depression, PTSD, personality disorders.

6395 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Clinical findings incompatible with recognized neurological conditions
6396 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Symptom causes significant distress or impairment
6397 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Not better explained by another condition
6398 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 💊 TREATMENT OF PNES
6399 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | The mainstay of treatment is psychotherapy, NOT antiepileptic drugs (AEDs).
6400 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 1. 📢 Education
6401 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Explain that seizures are real but not due to epilepsy.
6402 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Avoid implying that the patient is “faking” the condition.
6403 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 2. 🧠 Psychotherapy
6404 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) – most evidence-based.
6405 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Trauma-focused therapy – if PTSD or abuse history is present.
6406 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Family therapy – especially in adolescents.
6407 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 3. 💊 Medications
6408 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Antidepressants or anxiolytics – if psychiatric comorbidity (e.g., SSRIs for depression).
6409 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Avoid AEDs unless epilepsy is confirmed.
6410 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 4. 👩‍⚕️ Multidisciplinary approach

6412 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Address social stressors (abuse, school pressure, domestic violence)
6413 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 5. 🔁 Follow-up and Monitoring
6414 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Regular follow-up to monitor reduction in episodes.
6415 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Reinforce progress and support coping strategies.

7259 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 📊 ETIOLOGY (Causes of Myocarditis)
7260 [PARA] Normal                         | A. Infectious Causes (most common worldwide)
7261 [PARA] Normal                         |  Viral examples: Coxsackievirus B1–B5 ),Adenovirus ,Parvovirus B19,Human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6),HIV ,Hepatitis C, CMV, In
7262 [PARA] Normal                         |  Bacterial: Streptococcus pyogenes (rheumatic fever),Corynebacterium diphtheriae, Borrelia burgdorferi (Lyme disease), M
7263 [PARA] Normal                         | Protozoal & Parasitic: Trypanosoma cruzi (Chagas disease),Toxoplasma gondii

7265 [PARA] Normal                         | B. Non-Infectious Causes
7266 [PARA] Normal                         | Autoimmune Disorders: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), Rheumatoid arthritis (RA), Sarcoidosis, Giant cell myocarditis
7267 [PARA] Normal                         |  Drug-induced (hypersensitivity or toxicity): Clozapine, Methyldopa, Checkpoint inhibitors (e.g., nivolumab), Chemothera
7268 [PARA] Normal                         |  Toxins: Alcohol, Heavy metals, Catecholamines (stress-induced)
7269 [PARA] Normal                         |  Post-vaccine myocarditis: Rare, associated with mRNA COVID-19 vaccines, especially in young males

7271 [PARA] Normal                         | 
7272 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 🔬 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY
7273 [PARA] Normal                         | Phases of Myocarditis Development
7274 [PARA] Normal                         | 1. Viral Entry and Injury (Acute Phase)
7275 [PARA] Normal                         | Virus enters cardiomyocytes via receptors (e.g., Coxsackievirus receptor, ACE2)
7276 [PARA] Normal                         | Direct cytopathic effect → cell death
7277 [PARA] Normal                         | Activation of innate immunity
7278 [PARA] Normal                         | 2. Autoimmune Phase (Subacute Phase)
7279 [PARA] Normal                         | Molecular mimicry: host immune system targets cardiac antigens
7280 [PARA] Normal                         | CD4+/CD8+ T-cell infiltration
7281 [PARA] Normal                         | Release of cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1, IL-6)
7282 [PARA] Normal                         | 3. Chronic Phase
7283 [PARA] Normal                         | Persistent inflammation
7284 [PARA] Normal                         | Fibrosis and remodeling → Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM)
7285 [PARA] Normal                         | Irreversible heart failure
7286 [PARA] Normal                         |

7801 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 3. ❤️ Symptoms of Heart Failure
7802 [PARA] Heading 4                      | 🫁 Pulmonary Congestion (Left-sided HF)
7803 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Does the child get short of breath easily (e.g., during feeding, crying, or walking)?
7804 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Does he/she have a persistent cough, wheeze, or rapid breathing?
7805 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any recurrent chest infections?
7806 [PARA] Heading 4                      | 🫀 Systemic Congestion (Right-sided HF)
7807 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is there any swelling in the legs, abdomen, or around the eyes?
7808 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Have you noticed abdominal distension or early satiety?
7809 [PARA] Heading 4                      | 🍼 Feeding Difficulties in Infants
7810 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Does the child get tired while feeding or sweat during feeds?
7811 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is the baby not finishing bottles or takes a long time to feed?
7812 [PARA] Heading 4                      | 🏃 Exercise Intolerance (in older children)
7813 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Does the child keep up with peers during play?
7814 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any early fatigue, palpitations, or chest pain with exertion?
7815 [PARA] Heading 4                      | 💤 Signs of Poor Perfusion
7816 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is the child often drowsy, irritable, or lethargic?
7817 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is there poor weight gain or failure to thrive?

8221 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 1. 🫀 Carditis / Rheumatic Heart Disease (RHD)
8222 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Ask for symptoms of valvulitis, myocarditis, or pericarditis:
8223 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Does the child get tired easily during play or activity?
8224 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has there been any chest pain or tightness?
8225 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is the child breathing fast or getting short of breath easily?
8226 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any swelling of the legs or face?
8227 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has the child fainted or had episodes of palpitations?
8228 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any episodes of bluish lips or fainting?
8229 [PARA] Normal                         | 
8230 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 2. 🦴 Polyarthritis
8231 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has the child complained of pain or swelling in any joints?
8232 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Did the joint pain move from one joint to another (migratory)?
8233 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Were the joints red, hot, or swollen?
8234 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Did pain improve with rest and worsen with movement?
8235 [PARA] Normal                         | 
8236 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 3. 🧠 Sydenham’s Chorea
8237 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has the child had any unusual jerky movements or unsteady walking?
8238 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has there been clumsiness, difficulty holding objects, or handwriting changes?
8239 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any emotional changes, crying spells, or mood swings?
8240 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Are the symptoms worse with stress and go away during sleep?
8241 [PARA] Normal                         |

8439 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 1. Precordial Findings
8440 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Pericardial friction rub
8441 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | High-pitched, scratchy/squeaky sound best heard at the left lower sternal border
8442 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Heard during end expiration, and with the child leaning forward
8443 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Can be triphasic (systolic + 2 diastolic components)
8444 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Muffled or distant heart sounds – suggestive of pericardial effusion/tamponade
8445 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Displaced apex beat – usually not displaced in pericarditis (but may be if cardiomegaly or massive effusion)
8446 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Tachycardia – persistent, even at rest
8447 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 2. Pulse & Blood Pressure

8449 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Low pulse volume – may indicate tamponade

8451 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Pulsus paradoxus – check during quiet respiration

9276 [PARA] Normal                         | 
9277 [PARA] Normal                         | 1. King’s College Criteria (Prognosis in Acute Liver Failure)
9278 [PARA] Normal                         | A. Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)–Induced Acute Liver Failure
9279 [PARA] Normal                         | Poor prognosis if ANY ONE is present:
9280 [PARA] Normal                         | Arterial pH < 7.3 (after fluid resuscitation)
9281 [PARA] Normal                         | OR
9282 [PARA] Normal                         | ALL of the following:
9283 [PARA] Normal                         | INR > 6.5 (PT > 100 seconds)
9284 [PARA] Normal                         | Serum creatinine > 300 μmol/L (≈ 3.4 mg/dL
9285 [PARA] Normal                         | Grade III or IV hepatic encephalopathy
9286 [PARA] Normal                         | 
9287 [PARA] Normal                         | B. Non-Paracetamol Acute Liver Failure
9288 [PARA] Normal                         | Poor prognosis if ANY ONE is present:
9289 [PARA] Normal                         | INR > 6.5 (PT > 100 seconds)
9290 [PARA] Normal                         | OR
9291 [PARA] Normal                         | ANY THREE of the following five:
9292 [PARA] Normal                         | Age <10 years or >40 years
9293 [PARA] Normal                         | Etiology: non-A non-B hepatitis, halothane, idiosyncratic drug reaction
9294 [PARA] Normal                         | Duration of jaundice >7 days before encephalopathy
9295 [PARA] Normal                         | INR > 3.5 (PT > 50 seconds)
9296 [PARA] Normal                         | Serum bilirubin > 300 μmol/L (~17.5 mg/dL)
9297 [PARA] Normal                         | 
9298 [PARA] Normal                         | 2. PELD Score (Paediatric End-Stage Liver Disease Score – Chronic Liver Disease)
9299 [PARA] Normal                         | Used in:
9300 [PARA] Normal                         | Children < 12 years
9301 [PARA] Normal                         | Chronic liver disease
9302 [PARA] Normal                         | Transplant prioritization
9303 [PARA] Normal                         | PELD Formula
9304 [PARA] Normal                         | PELD = 0.436 (Age < 1yr) + 0.667 (Growth failure) + 0.480 ln (bilirubin) + 1.857 ln (Albumin)
9305 [PARA] Normal                         | Interpretation
9306 [PARA] Normal                         | Higher score = higher mortality risk
9307 [PARA] Normal                         | PELD ≥ 15–20 → consider transplant referral
9308 [PARA] Normal                         | 
9309 [PARA] Normal                         | 3. Practical Bedside Prognostic Markers in Children
9310 [PARA] Normal                         | (INR + Encephalopathy — commonly used in resource-limited settings)
9311 [TABLE] 5x2                            | Parameter | Poor Prognosis Indicator
9312 [PARA] Normal                         | High-Yield Practical Rule

9314 [PARA] Normal                         | King’s College → acute liver failure
9315 [PARA] Normal                         | PELD → chronic liver disease in children

9446 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Normal growth and development otherwise?

9568 [PARA] Normal                         | ✅ 2. Questions to Rule Out Causes of FTT
9569 [PARA] Normal                         | Use the mnemonic "I D-I-G C-A-U-S-E" to remember the categories:
9570 [PARA] Normal                         | 
9571 [PARA] Normal                         | 🧩 A. Inadequate Intake (I)
9572 [PARA] Normal                         | “Is there enough food in the home?”
9573 [PARA] Normal                         | “Any feeding difficulties or distractions during meals?”
9574 [PARA] Normal                         | “Does the child stop feeding early, choke, or cough?”
9575 [PARA] Normal                         | 
9576 [PARA] Normal                         | 🦠 B. Disease – Chronic Illness (D)
9577 [PARA] Normal                         | “Has your child had frequent infections (cough, diarrhea, fever)?”
9578 [PARA] Normal                         | “Any diagnosis of asthma, congenital heart disease, kidney issues, or TB?”
9579 [PARA] Normal                         | 
9580 [PARA] Normal                         | 🌱 C. Interaction / Psychosocial Deprivation (I)
9581 [PARA] Normal                         | “Who takes care of your child during the day?”
9582 [PARA] Normal                         | “Are there many children at home competing for food or attention?”
9583 [PARA] Normal                         | “Any history of neglect, domestic violence, or maternal depression?”
9584 [PARA] Normal                         | 
9585 [PARA] Normal                         | 🌾 D. Gastrointestinal Causes (G)
9586 [PARA] Normal                         | “Any history of frequent diarrhea, constipation, or vomiting?”
9587 [PARA] Normal                         | “Are the stools bulky, oily, or foul-smelling?” (malabsorption)
9588 [PARA] Normal                         | 
9589 [PARA] Normal                         | 🧬 E. Congenital/Metabolic Disorders (C)
9590 [PARA] Normal                         | “Any family history of growth delay, thyroid disorders, or genetic conditions?”
9591 [PARA] Normal                         | “Was the child’s newborn screening normal?”
9592 [PARA] Normal                         | 
9593 [PARA] Normal                         | 🍼 F. Allergies/Intolerances (A)
9594 [PARA] Normal                         | “Any food allergies or intolerance (e.g., lactose, cow’s milk)?”
9595 [PARA] Normal                         | “Any rash, vomiting, or diarrhea after specific foods?”
9596 [PARA] Normal                         | 
9597 [PARA] Normal                         | ☠️ G. Urinary Losses / Renal (U)
9598 [PARA] Normal                         | “Has your child had swelling, frothy urine, or reduced urine output?” (Nephrotic syndrome)
9599 [PARA] Normal                         | 
9600 [PARA] Normal                         | 🩸 H. Systemic Infections (S)
9601 [PARA] Normal                         | “Has your child been treated for HIV, TB, or hepatitis?”
9602 [PARA] Normal                         | “Any exposure to people with chronic infections?”
9603 [PARA] Normal                         | 
9604 [PARA] Normal                         | ⚠️ I. Endocrine or Hormonal (E)
9605 [PARA] Normal                         | “Any signs of early or delayed puberty?”
9606 [PARA] Normal                         | “Does your child seem too sleepy or too active?”
9607 [PARA] Normal                         | “Any family history of diabetes, thyroid, or adrenal issues?”

10126 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Rhinitis is the inflammation of the nasal mucosa, often presenting with nasal congestion, sneezing, rhinorrhea, and itch

10157 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Otitis media (especially in children)
10158 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Mouth breathing (adenoidal face in chronic cases)
10159 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Epistaxis (from constant nose blowing or medicamentosa)
10160 [PARA] Heading 2                      | TIPS & FACTS
10161 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Allergic rhinitis is often associated with asthma and eczema (atopic triad).
10162 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Rhinitis medicamentosa is rebound congestion due to overuse of topical nasal decongestants (e.g., oxymetazoline).
10163 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Atrophic rhinitis can occur post nasal/sinus surgery or due to infections like leprosy, syphilis.
10164 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Nasal eosinophilia supports allergic rhinitis; absence suggests vasomotor rhinitis.
10165 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 
10166 [PARA] Heading 2                      |  SINUSITIS (Rhinosinusitis)
10167 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Inflammation of one or more of the paranasal sinuses, often due to infection, allergy, or autoimmune processes.
10168 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 🦠 TYPES 
10169 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Acute (<4 weeks) – often viral or bacterial
10170 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Bacterial – secondary to viral (S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae)
10171 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Chronic (>12 weeks) – recurrent episodes or unresolved inflammation
10172 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Complex – fungal (aspergillus), invasive
10173 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Fungal sinusitis – common in immunocompromised (e.g., diabetics)
10174 [PARA] Normal                         |

10225 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | In chronic sinusitis, CT shows mucosal thickening, polyps, or opacification

12675 [PARA] Normal                         | May indicate advanced stage or systemic spread

12680 [PARA] Normal                         | Tenderness if bowel obstruction or rapid tumor growth

12685 [PARA] Normal                         | Delayed milestones (if chronic illness)

13251 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 🔹 Why DKA occurs in some patients with T2D (5–25%)
13252 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Although diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is classically associated with type 1 diabetes (T1D) due to absolute insulin defici
13253 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 1. Relative Insulin Deficiency
13254 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Some patients with T2D (especially lean individuals, adolescents, or certain ethnic groups) may present with marked β-ce
13255 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | This leads to relative or near-absolute insulin deficiency, enough to cause lipolysis → ketone production → acidosis.
13256 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 2. Ketosis-Prone Type 2 Diabetes (“Flatbush Diabetes”)
13257 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Seen more often in African, Hispanic, and Asian populations.
13258 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Patients present with DKA like T1D but later behave metabolically like T2D.
13259 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | They often recover β-cell function after the acute episode and can sometimes be managed without insulin long term.
13260 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 3. Precipitating Factors
13261 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Even in “typical” T2D, stressful conditions can increase insulin demand and overwhelm residual β-cell function, precipit
13262 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Severe infections (pneumonia, UTI, sepsis).
13263 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Myocardial infarction, stroke.
13264 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Pancreatitis.
13265 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Use of certain drugs (e.g., corticosteroids, atypical antipsychotics, SGLT2 inhibitors).
13266 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 4. SGLT2 Inhibitor–Induced Euglycemic DKA
13267 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Newer antidiabetic drugs (SGLT2 inhibitors) can cause DKA even in T2D.
13268 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Mechanism: increased glucagon-to-insulin ratio, enhanced ketogenesis, dehydration, reduced renal clearance of ketones.
13269 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Notably, these cases may have near-normal glucose (“euglycemic DKA”).
13270 [PARA] Heading 3                      | 5. Misclassification of Diabetes
13271 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Some patients diagnosed as “T2D” may actually have latent autoimmune diabetes of adults (LADA) or atypical forms of T1D,

14074 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 1. Etiologic Classification
14075 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | From the perspective of cause, AKI can result from:
14076 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Ischemic causes – hypoperfusion, shock.
14077 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Toxic causes – drugs, contrast agents, poisons.
14078 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Inflammatory causes – glomerulonephritis, vasculitis, infections.
14079 [PARA] Normal                         | 
14080 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 2. Mechanistic / Pathophysiologic Classification
14081 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Based on the underlying mechanism:
14082 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Functional (Prerenal) AKI
14083 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Kidneys structurally normal.
14084 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Occurs due to hypoperfusion (e.g., dehydration, shock).
14085 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Rapidly reversible with restoration of renal perfusion.
14086 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | If untreated → progresses to intrinsic AKI.
14087 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Intrinsic (Renal) AKI
14088 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Due to structural kidney damage.
14089 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Causes: prolonged ischemia, nephrotoxins, sepsis, intrinsic renal diseases (e.g., glomerulonephritis).
14090 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | No specific curative therapy once established — only supportive care (medical management & dialysis).
14091 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Postrenal AKI
14092 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Due to urinary tract obstruction (stones, tumors, posterior urethral valves).
14093 [PARA] Normal                         | 
14094 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 3. Clinical Setting Classification
14095 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Based on where AKI is acquired:
14096 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Community-acquired AKI
14097 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Commonly prerenal (hypoperfusion-related).
14098 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | May result from primary renal diseases (e.g., post-streptococcal GN, hemolytic-uremic syndrome).
14099 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Hospital-acquired AKI
14100 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Usually multifactorial.
14101 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Seen in “at-risk” critically ill patients with multiple comorbidities.
14102 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Nephrotoxin-mediated AKI may occur in both community and hospital settings.
14103 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Risk is higher with exposure to ≥3 nephrotoxic drugs (threshold effect).

14393 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 🚼 VESICOURETERIC REFLUX (VUR) 
14394 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | VUR is the retrograde flow of urine from the bladder into the ureters ± renal pelvis, due to an incompetent vesicoureter
14395 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | It predisposes to urinary tract infections (UTIs) and renal scarring, especially in children.
14396 [PARA] Normal                         | 
14397 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 🧠 PHYSIOLOGY OF REFLUX
14398 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Normally, the intramural segment of the ureter acts as a valve.
14399 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | In VUR, this segment is shortened or misaligned, failing to close during bladder contraction → urine refluxes back.

14964 [PARA] Normal                         | 🌡️ WHAT IS MICROCYTIC ANAEMIA?
14965 [PARA] Normal                         | Microcytic anaemia is defined as anaemia (low haemoglobin) with mean corpuscular volume (MCV) < 80 fL in adults or below
14966 [PARA] Normal                         | 
14967 [PARA] Normal                         | 🧠 CAUSES OF MICROCYTIC ANAEMIA — Mnemonic: TICS
14968 [TABLE] 6x3                            | Mnemonic | Cause | Mechanism
14969 [PARA] Normal                         | 
14970 [PARA] Normal                         | 📊 DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS TABLE — Microcytic Anaemia in Children
14971 [TABLE] 9x6                            | Feature | Iron Deficiency Anaemia | Thalassemia Trait | Anaemia of Chronic Disease | Sideroblastic A…
14972 [PARA] Normal                         | 
14973 [PARA] Normal                         | 🔬 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY QUICK LOOK
14974 [PARA] Normal                         | 1. Iron Deficiency Anaemia (IDA)
14975 [PARA] Normal                         | ↓ Iron → ↓ Heme → ↓ Hb → microcytosis
14976 [PARA] Normal                         | Common in infants < 1 year (low iron stores, poor diet), adolescents (growth spurt, menstruation)
14977 [PARA] Normal                         | 2. Thalassemia Trait (α or β)
14978 [PARA] Normal                         | Genetic defect → reduced globin chains → microcytic cells despite normal iron stores
14979 [PARA] Normal                         | 3. Anaemia of Chronic Disease
14980 [PARA] Normal                         | Inflammation → ↑ Hepcidin → blocks iron absorption/release → functional iron deficiency
14981 [PARA] Normal                         | 4. Sideroblastic Anaemia
14982 [PARA] Normal                         | Iron available but defective incorporation into Hb → iron-laden mitochondria seen as ring sideroblasts
14983 [PARA] Normal                         | 5. Lead Poisoning
14984 [PARA] Normal                         | Lead inhibits enzymes in heme synthesis (e.g. ferrochelatase) → anaemia + neurotoxicity
14985 [PARA] Normal                         | 
14986 [PARA] Normal                         | 🔍 HISTORY & PHYSICAL EXAMINATION CLUES
14987 [TABLE] 7x2                            | Symptom / Sign | Implication
14988 [PARA] Normal                         | 
14989 [PARA] Normal                         | 🧪 DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP
14990 [PARA] Normal                         | Initial Tests:
14991 [PARA] Normal                         | FBC with RBC indices (MCV, RDW)
14992 [PARA] Normal                         | Blood film
14993 [PARA] Normal                         | Reticulocyte count
14994 [PARA] Normal                         | Serum iron studies (Iron, TIBC, Ferritin, Transferrin saturation)
14995 [PARA] Normal                         | CRP/ESR (inflammatory markers)
14996 [PARA] Normal                         | Hb Electrophoresis
14997 [PARA] Normal                         | Lead level (if suspected)
14998 [PARA] Normal                         | Bone marrow (rarely needed)
14999 [PARA] Normal                         |

15007 [PARA] Normal                         | Nutritional education (especially iron-rich foods: meat, green veggies, legumes)
15008 [PARA] Normal                         | Iron supplements during high-risk periods (infancy, adolescence)
15009 [PARA] Normal                         | Lead screening in high-risk environments
15010 [PARA] Normal                         | Family screening for thalassemia
15011 [PARA] Normal                         | Deworming in areas with high helminth burden

15121 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 🧬 WHAT IS SICKLE CELL ANAEMIA?
15122 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Sickle cell anaemia is a hereditary haemoglobinopathy characterized by:
15123 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Mutation in the β-globin gene (substitution of valine for glutamic acid at position 6)
15124 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Formation of abnormal haemoglobin S (HbS)
15125 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Under low oxygen or stress conditions, HbS polymerizes, causing sickling of RBCs
15126 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | 👉 It is autosomal recessive and common in sub-Saharan Africa, India, and Mediterranean populations.
15127 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15128 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 🔬 GENETIC VARIANTS
15129 [TABLE] 6x3                            | Type | Genotype | Clinical Severity
15130 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15131 [PARA] Heading 2                      | PATHOPHYSIOLOGY 
15132 [PARA] Normal                         | As a result of a single amino acid substitution (valine for glutamic acid at the β6 position), sickle hemoglobin
15133 [PARA] Normal                         | crystallizes and forms a gel in the deoxygenated state. When
15134 [PARA] Normal                         | reoxygenated, the sickle hemoglobin is normally soluble.
15135 [PARA] Normal                         | The so-called reversible sickle cell is capable of entering the
15136 [PARA] Normal                         | microcirculation. As the oxygen is extracted and saturation
15137 [PARA] Normal                         | declines, sickling may occur, occluding the microvasculature.
15138 [PARA] Normal                         | The surrounding tissue undergoes infarction, inducing pain
15139 [PARA] Normal                         | and dysfunction. This sickling phenomenon is exacerbated by
15140 [PARA] Normal                         | hypoxia, acidosis, fever, hypothermia, and dehydration.

15175 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Acute sickle cell crises are sudden episodes of clinical deterioration in patients with sickle cell disease (SCD), trigg
15176 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Hypoxia, dehydration, infection, cold, stress, etc.
15177 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | They are characterized by acute pain, anaemia, or organ dysfunction, and often require emergency management.

15257 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Rare, immune-mediated post-transfusion haemolysis
15258 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Can occur days after transfusion
15259 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Features:
15260 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Fever, fatigue

15268 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 6. BONE MARROW SEQUESTRATION CRISIS
15269 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Bone marrow sequestration crisis is an acute, life-threatening condition in which there is massive pooling of blood with
15270 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Sudden severe anemia,
15271 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Circulatory collapse (shock), and
15272 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Sometimes bone pain.
15273 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | It is similar in mechanism to splenic sequestration, but instead of the spleen, the bone marrow becomes the site of bloo
15274 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | May occur with parvovirus B19 infection (can also cause aplastic crisis).
15275 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Clinical Features
15276 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Onset: Sudden and severe.
15277 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Symptoms:
15278 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Sudden pallor and weakness
15279 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Bone pain, especially in long bones or vertebrae
15280 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Dyspnea, tachycardia, dizziness
15281 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Collapse or shock in severe cases
15282 [PARA] Heading 4                      | Signs:
15283 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Severe pallor
15284 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Tachycardia, hypotension
15285 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Bone tenderness
15286 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | May have warm extremities and bounding pulse early, then cold clammy skin if shock develops
15287 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Investigations
15288 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Full blood count:
15289 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Marked drop in Hb (acute anemia)
15290 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Reticulocytosis (unless aplastic crisis coexists)
15291 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | White cell count and platelets may be elevated due to stress response.
15292 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Peripheral blood film:
15293 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Sickle cells, target cells.
15294 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Bone marrow aspiration/biopsy (rarely needed acutely):
15295 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Shows engorged sinusoids and trapped red cells.
15296 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Treatment
15297 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Emergency management required!
15298 [PARA] Heading 4                      | 1. Resuscitation
15299 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Oxygen therapy
15300 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Intravenous fluids — to restore circulating volume.
15301 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Monitor vital signs closely (BP, HR, urine output).
15302 [PARA] Heading 4                      | 2. Transfusion
15303 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Simple blood transfusion to raise Hb and restore oxygen-carrying capacity.
15304 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Exchange transfusion may be indicated in severe cases to reduce sickled cells.
15305 [PARA] Heading 4                      | 3. Pain control
15306 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Analgesics (paracetamol, opioids if severe).
15307 [PARA] Heading 4                      | 4. Treat precipitating factors
15308 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Antibiotics if infection suspected.
15309 [PARA] Heading 4                      | 5. Monitor for complications
15310 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Shock, multiorgan failure, or recurrence.

15349 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 🧬 WHAT IS THALASSAEMIA?
15350 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Thalassaemia is a group of inherited blood disorders caused by defective synthesis of one or more globin chains of hemog
15351 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | There are two major types based on which chain is affected:

15353 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | β-thalassaemia: ↓ β-globin chain synthesis
15354 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | 👉 It leads to microcytic hypochromic anaemia, ineffective erythropoiesis, and haemolysis.

15441 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 🧬 WHAT IS VON WILLEBRAND DISEASE?

15443 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Platelet adhesion at sites of vascular injury

15451 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Most common inherited bleeding disorder (~1% of the population)

15485 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 🩸 DISSEMINATED INTRAVASCULAR COAGULATION (DIC) IN CHILDREN
15486 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15487 [PARA] Heading 2                      | What is DIC?
15488 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | DIC is an acquired systemic disorder characterized by widespread activation of coagulation pathways, leading to:
15489 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Formation of microvascular thrombi
15490 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Consumption of platelets and clotting factors (consumption coagulopathy)
15491 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Secondary activation of fibrinolysis
15492 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Resulting in simultaneous thrombosis and bleeding
15493 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15494 [PARA] Heading 2                      | ⚠️ PATHOPHYSIOLOGY
15495 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Trigger (infection, trauma, malignancy, etc.) → massive release of tissue factor or other procoagulants
15496 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Activation of coagulation cascade → widespread fibrin deposition
15497 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Consumption of clotting factors & platelets → bleeding tendency
15498 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Secondary fibrinolysis → increased fibrin degradation products (FDPs) and D-dimers
15499 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Microvascular thrombosis → organ ischemia and failure
15500 [PARA] Normal                         |

15523 [PARA] Heading 2                      | ⚠️ SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS IN CHILDREN
15524 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | DIC can develop rapidly in neonates, especially with sepsis or birth asphyxia.
15525 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | High index of suspicion in children with severe infections, trauma, or malignancy.
15526 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Avoid over-transfusion which may worsen microvascular thrombosis.
15527 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Monitor closely for organ dysfunction — kidneys, lungs, brain.

15533 [PARA] Heading 1                      | History Taking in a Child with Microcytic Anaemia
15534 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15535 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 1. Presenting Complaints
15536 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | When did the symptoms start?
15537 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is the child feeling more tired or weak than usual?
15538 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any history of paleness?
15539 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has the child noticed any shortness of breath or rapid heartbeat?
15540 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any episodes of dizziness or fainting?
15541 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any history of easy bruising or bleeding?
15542 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any abdominal pain or swelling?
15543 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has the child had any episodes of dark or bloody stools?
15544 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15545 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 2. Dietary History
15546 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | What does the child usually eat?
15547 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Does the child consume iron-rich foods (meat, leafy greens)?
15548 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any history of pica (eating non-food substances like dirt or clay)?
15549 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is the child breastfed or formula-fed? For how long?
15550 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is there a history of cow’s milk intake exceeding recommended amounts (can cause iron deficiency)?
15551 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15552 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 3. Past Medical History
15553 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has the child had previous episodes of anaemia?
15554 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any history of blood transfusions?
15555 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | History of infections, especially chronic or recurrent?
15556 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | History of chronic illnesses (e.g., chronic kidney disease, inflammatory bowel disease)?
15557 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any known inherited blood disorders in the child?
15558 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15559 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 4. Family History
15560 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any family history of anaemia or blood disorders (thalassemia, sickle cell disease)?
15561 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any family members requiring blood transfusions?
15562 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Ethnic background (some hemoglobinopathies more common in certain populations)?
15563 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15564 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 5. Growth and Development
15565 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Is the child growing normally?
15566 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any developmental delays?
15567 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any history of failure to thrive?
15568 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15569 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 6. Symptoms to Rule Out Specific Causes
15570 [PARA] Heading 3                      | For Iron Deficiency Anaemia (IDA):
15571 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any chronic blood loss (e.g., heavy menstrual bleeding in adolescent girls)?
15572 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any history of gastrointestinal symptoms (pain, diarrhea, constipation)?
15573 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | History of hookworm infection or other parasitic infestations?
15574 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has the child received iron supplementation before?
15575 [PARA] Heading 3                      | For Thalassemia and Other Hemoglobinopathies:
15576 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any family history of hemoglobinopathies?
15577 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any jaundice or history of gallstones?
15578 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any history of frequent infections or splenomegaly?
15579 [PARA] Heading 3                      | For Lead Poisoning:
15580 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any exposure to lead paint, contaminated water, or soil?
15581 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any neurobehavioral symptoms like irritability or learning difficulties?
15582 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15583 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 7. Complications
15584 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has the child experienced any breathlessness on exertion or at rest?
15585 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any recurrent infections (suggesting immunosuppression or splenic dysfunction)?
15586 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any bone pain or fractures?
15587 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any swelling or pain in joints (possible in hemoglobinopathies)?
15588 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Any history of heart problems or palpitations?
15589 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has the child had any bleeding episodes (nosebleeds, gum bleeding)?
