15591 [PARA] Heading 1                      | Examination Findings in a Child with Microcytic Anaemia
15592 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15593 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 1. General Appearance
15594 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Pallor: Most common sign — especially noticeable in conjunctiva, palms, nail beds, and oral mucosa
15595 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Tachycardia and tachypnea: Due to compensatory increased cardiac output
15596 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Growth parameters: May show stunted growth or failure to thrive in chronic anaemia
15597 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Jaundice: May suggest hemolysis (e.g., thalassemia) or chronic blood loss
15598 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Clubbing: Rare, but may be present with chronic hypoxia or iron deficiency
15599 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Facial features:
15600 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Frontal bossing or maxillary prominence (“chipmunk facies”) in thalassemia major due to marrow expansion
15601 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15602 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 2. Vital Signs
15603 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Pulse: Tachycardia
15604 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Blood pressure: May be low in severe anaemia or bleeding
15605 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Respiratory rate: Increased if severe anaemia
15606 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15607 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 3. Skin
15608 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Pallor (palms, soles, nail beds)
15609 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Petechiae or bruising: May indicate bleeding tendency or thrombocytopenia
15610 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Xerosis or angular stomatitis: Common in iron deficiency
15611 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Koilonychia (spoon nails): Suggestive of iron deficiency anaemia
15612 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Jaundice: Suggests hemolytic anaemia
15613 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15614 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 4. Head and Neck
15615 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Conjunctival pallor
15616 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Glossitis: Smooth, inflamed tongue in iron deficiency
15617 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Angular stomatitis or cheilitis
15618 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Lymphadenopathy: May suggest infection or malignancy
15619 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Hepatosplenomegaly:
15620 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Common in hemolytic anaemias like thalassemia
15621 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | May also suggest chronic infection or malignancy
15622 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15623 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 5. Cardiovascular System
15624 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Tachycardia
15625 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Flow murmur: A soft systolic murmur due to increased blood flow (hyperdynamic circulation)
15626 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Signs of heart failure: In severe, chronic anaemia
15627 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15628 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 6. Abdominal Examination
15629 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Hepatomegaly and splenomegaly:
15630 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Suggests hemolysis (e.g., thalassemia) or extramedullary hematopoiesis
15631 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Palpable masses: May indicate malignancy or other causes
15632 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15633 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 7. Musculoskeletal System
15634 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Bone deformities:
15635 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Especially in thalassemia major (marrow expansion) causing bossing of the skull or prominent cheekbones
15636 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Bone tenderness or fractures: Suggests bone marrow disease or metabolic bone disease
15637 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15638 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 8. Neurological Examination
15639 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Check for any neurological deficits (important if lead poisoning is suspected)
15640 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Signs of developmental delay or cognitive impairment
15641 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15642 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 9. Other Signs
15643 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Pica: May be reported during history or seen as dirt under nails
15644 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Signs of chronic disease: such as lymphadenopathy or cachexia if underlying infection or malignancy

15702 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Jaundice: Mild to moderate, indicating hemolysis or ineffective erythropoiesis
15703 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Growth retardation: Especially in chronic or nutritional causes
15704 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Cachexia or malnutrition: May be present in severe folate or B12 deficiency
15705 [PARA] Normal                         |

15709 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Blood pressure: Usually normal unless complicated by cardiac failure
15710 [PARA] Normal                         |

15712 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Pallor
15713 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Petechiae or bruising: Suggestive of thrombocytopenia or bone marrow failure
15714 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Hyperpigmentation: Rare, may be seen in some congenital causes or nutritional deficiencies
15715 [PARA] Normal                         |

15717 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Glossitis: Beefy, smooth, and sore tongue commonly seen in B12 and folate deficiency

15719 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Lymphadenopathy: May indicate malignancy or infection
15720 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Pallor of conjunctiva

15722 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 5. Neurological Examination
15723 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Peripheral neuropathy: Loss of vibration and proprioception, stocking-glove sensory loss in B12 deficiency
15724 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Ataxia: Unsteady gait or difficulty walking
15725 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Hyporeflexia or hyperreflexia: Depending on severity and level of involvement
15726 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Developmental delays or cognitive impairment: Especially in infants and young children with B12 deficiency
15727 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15728 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 6. Cardiovascular System
15729 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Tachycardia and flow murmur: Common in anaemia
15730 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Signs of heart failure: In chronic or severe anaemia
15731 [PARA] Normal                         | 
15732 [PARA] Heading 2                      | 7. Abdominal Examination
15733 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Hepatosplenomegaly: May be present in hemolytic causes or bone marrow disorders

16566 [PARA] Heading 1                      | Use of Inotropes in the Management of Sepsis
16567 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | In sepsis, especially septic shock, circulatory failure occurs due to vasodilation, reduced systemic vascular resistance
16568 [PARA] Normal                         | 
16569 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 1. When to Start Inotropes
16570 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Start inotropes/vasopressors when:
16571 [PARA] Heading 3                      | ✓ Persistent hypotension (MAP < 65 mmHg) despite adequate fluid resuscitation (30 mL/kg crystalloid)
16572 [PARA] Heading 3                      | ✓ Signs of hypoperfusion:
16573 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Altered mental status
16574 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Oliguria (<0.5 mL/kg/hr)
16575 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Lactate > 2 mmol/L
16576 [PARA] Normal                         | 
16577 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 2. First-Line Agent: Norepinephrine
16578 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Drug: Norepinephrine (Noradrenaline)
16579 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Role: Vasopressor of choice for septic shock
16580 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Strong α1 agonist → vasoconstriction → ↑SVR → ↑MAP
16581 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Mild β1 effect → slight increase in cardiac output
16582 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Target MAP: 65–70 mmHg
16583 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Dose: 0.05–1 µg/kg/min IV (titrated in ICU settings)
16584 [PARA] Normal                         | 
16585 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 3. Add Vasopressin if Needed
16586 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Drug: Vasopressin (ADH)
16587 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Role: Second-line agent added when norepinephrine requirement is high
16588 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Restores vascular tone in vasodilatory shock
16589 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Reduces norepinephrine dose requirement (norepinephrine-sparing)
16590 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Dose: 0.03 units/min (fixed dose)
16591 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Do NOT use vasopressin alone as initial vasopressor.
16592 [PARA] Normal                         | 
16593 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 4. When to Add Inotropes
16594 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Inotropes are added when myocardial dysfunction is present:
16595 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Indications:
16596 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Low cardiac output despite adequate MAP
16597 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Ejection fraction < 40% on echo
16598 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Persistent tissue hypoperfusion with normal or high MAP
16599 [PARA] Normal                         | 
16600 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 5. First-Line Inotrope: Dobutamine
16601 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Drug: Dobutamine
16602 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Role: Improves cardiac output in septic cardiomyopathy
16603 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | β1 agonist: ↑ contractility
16604 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | β2 agonist: mild vasodilation
16605 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Useful when lactate remains high despite fluids + vasopressors
16606 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Dose: 2–20 µg/kg/min IV infusion (Titrate based on cardiac output and perfusion)
16607 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Use cautiously: may cause hypotension — often combined with norepinephrine.
16608 [PARA] Normal                         | 
16609 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 6. Epinephrine (Adrenaline)
16610 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Role:
16611 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Alternative first-line or second-line agent when norepinephrine unavailable
16612 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Has both inotropic and vasoconstrictor effects
16613 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Increases lactate (β2 stimulation) — interpret lactate cautiously
16614 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Dose: 0.05–0.5 µg/kg/min IV
16615 [PARA] Normal                         | 
16616 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 7. Dopamine (Rarely Used Now)
16617 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Why rarely used:
16618 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Causes arrhythmias
16619 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Increases mortality versus norepinephrine in many studies
16620 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Reserved for bradycardic septic shock when heart rate is very low
16621 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Dose: 5–20 µg/kg/min IV
16622 [PARA] Normal                         | 
16623 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 8. Milrinone (Special Cases)
16624 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Role:
16625 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | PDE-3 inhibitor
16626 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Used in patients with septic shock + severe cardiac dysfunction, especially if on chronic β-blockers
16627 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Must monitor blood pressure (causes vasodilation)
16628 [PARA] Normal                         | 
16629 [PARA] Heading 1                      | 9. Monitoring During Inotropes
16630 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Continuous monitoring is essential:
16631 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Hemodynamics:
16632 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | BP (arterial line preferred)
16633 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Heart rate & rhythm
16634 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Urine output
16635 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Lactate trends
16636 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Echocardiography (to assess response)
16637 [PARA] Heading 3                      | Tissue Perfusion:
16638 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Capillary refill time
16639 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Mental status
16640 [PARA] Normal (Web)                   | Skin temperature
